Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on procurement readiness and the path forward: 

1) Procurement path:
- You mentioned procurement prefers PO for enterprise contracts but small pilot purchases may be done by card.
- Marketplace: you asked whether we’re available via cloud marketplaces (AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace) — short answer: we have an AWS Marketplace listing and can enable marketplace procurement for Dedicated/Private later in the process.

2) Security/compliance gating:
- SOC 2 Type II: Redwood has a current SOC 2 report; I’ll share the attestation and summarize what’s included.
- DPA: we have a standard DPA and a customer-editable template.
- Security questionnaire: sounds like you’ll run our info through your procurement/security form — Rafael + Nikhil can help with technical answers and provide evidence.

3) Timeline / ask from you:
- Can you confirm procurement’s preferred path (PO vs card) and whether marketplace procurement would speed the timeline?
- Please share any target dates and the security questionnaire (if you want us to complete it directly).

Next steps from our side (I’ll take action):
- Share SOC 2 attestation and DPA template (attached).
- Draft a short mutual action plan with milestones and a DocuSign path for signatures.
- Rafael/Nikhil to triage any technical questionnaire items.

Attachments: SOC2_Report_2026.pdf (attestation - redacted), Redwood_DPA_Template.docx, Mutual_Action_Plan_Acme.csv

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying items from procurement side:

- For pilots (~$5-10k) procurement will accept card transactions. For enterprise procurement we require a PO and a standard SOW/contract.
- Marketplace: if you can transact via AWS Marketplace with an invoiceable contract, that will shorten our legal review. Can you confirm the listing supports deferred billing / PO flow?
- SOC 2 / DPA: we’ll need the SOC 2 attestation and a DPA we can review. If possible we’d like a redline window of 3 business days — otherwise procurement will flag extended negotiation.

I’ve attached the initial procurement intake form — I’ll also send the security questionnaire to Rafael if that’s easiest.

- SOC 2: covers security and confidentiality controls for hosted API and Dedicated deployments; report is redacted for customer distribution. For deeper evidence we can arrange an on-site review or sign an NDA/SSAE request.
- DPA: our template is standard and includes data processing terms; we’re typically able to agree redlines within 3-5 business days for standard terms.
- Marketplace: AWS Marketplace supports contract/PO flows for customers who prefer invoice billing; I’m confirming the exact procurement flow for Acme and will share marketplace contract options.

Marissa

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for looping us in. Nikhil and I can take the security questionnaire. A few notes for your team to help speed up answers:

- Questionnaire scope: if the questionnaire is primarily org/process (policies, SOC attestations, vendor controls) we can return completed items within 3 business days. If it includes architecture-level items or requires evidence (network diagrams, vulnerability scans), that will take longer (5-10 business days).
- Evidence: we can provide redacted network diagrams, pen test summary, and SOC 2 reports under an NDA. Let us know if you want those now.
- Contract redlines: for standard pilot SOW + DPA we typically accept a 3-business-day redline window under your standard procurement process; for non-standard terms we’ll escalate to legal.

I’ll review the procurement intake form and start drafting answers.
